t.7.40.1: Having dismissed the bears, monkeys and Rākṣasas, the mighty-armed Rāma, together with his brothers, rejoiced, happy and at ease.
t.7.40.2: Then, at the time of afternoon, Rāghava, together with his brothers, heard a sweet voice spoken from the sky.
t.7.40.3: O gentle Rāma, look upon me with a gracious face; know me, O lord, to be Puṣpaka, come here from the peak of Kailāsa.
t.7.40.4: Having understood your command, O best of men, I went to Dhanada to attend upon him, and he spoke to me in reply.
t.7.40.5: You have been won by the great-souled lord of men, Rāghava, after he slew in battle the invincible Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas.
t.7.40.6: O gentle one, I too feel the highest joy now that the evil-souled Rāvaṇa has been slain together with his hosts, his sons, his ministers and his kinsmen.
t.7.40.7: You, who were won by the great-souled Rāma in Laṅkā, carry him alone, gentle one; I command you.
t.7.40.8: This is my highest wish, that you should carry the delight of the Rāghavas as the conveyance of the world; go, free from anxiety.
t.7.40.10: Saying "So be it," Kākutstha worshipped the Puṣpaka with parched grain and unbroken rice, with flowers, and with exceedingly fragrant perfumes.
t.7.40.9: Having understood that command of the great-souled Dhanada, I have come back to your presence once more; so, being such, accept me.
t.7.40.11: "Go now as you please, and come back whenever I remember you." Saying "So be it," Puṣpaka, dismissed once more by Rāma, departed for the direction it desired, Puṣpaka adorned with flowers.
t.7.40.12: When the Puṣpaka, of manifold nature, had thus vanished, Bharata, with joined palms, spoke these words to Raghunandana.
t.7.40.13: While you rule the kingdom, most wondrous things are seen: again and again the utterances of beings who are not human are heard.
t.7.40.14: Because mortals are free from illness, more than a month has now passed, and death does not come even to creatures worn out with age, O Rāghava.
t.7.40.15: Women give birth to sons, and men are handsome and well-formed; and, O King, the joy of the people dwelling in the city has grown exceedingly great.
t.7.40.16: And Vāsava sends down rain like nectar in its due season, and the winds too blow, pleasant to the touch and bestowing comfort.
t.7.40.17: "May such a one long be our king," O lord of men, so say the citizens in the city and the people throughout the countryside.
t.7.40.18: Hearing these exceedingly sweet words spoken by Bharata, Rāma, filled with joy, rejoiced greatly; happy, he delighted in his happiness.
